harbor.practice: Harbor: 8,000 employees + 1,200 customer tenants; 21,000 daily users × 6 requests, 14% in the peak hour, burst 2 → about 10 RPS at peak, about 60 in flight at 6 s each.
harbor.failure: Multiplying by a peak factor twice, or putting p99 latency into Little's law.

harbor.practice: Harbor's SLOs: 99.9% availability, p95 first token ≤ 1.5 s, sampled groundedness ≥ 95%, ≤ $0.01 per resolved question, each with a written measurement boundary.
harbor.failure: Treating a sampled judge score as a complete measurement of all production answers.

harbor.practice: Harbor's OCR backfill runs in its own pool and cannot take interactive inference slots; the assistant answers from the last consistent index while lag is visible.
harbor.failure: Splitting services but leaving them on one shared unbounded queue or saturated database.

harbor.practice: Harbor's hour-long imports return a job receipt; the query API reads only published index versions, never half-written chunks.
harbor.failure: A semantic cache keyed without permissions or source version.

harbor.practice: Harbor's gateway gives each tenant token-per-minute and concurrency quotas, weighted by estimated context size.
harbor.failure: Automatic fallback to a model that does not support the same tools or schema behaviour.

harbor.practice: When the model pool saturates, Harbor serves authorised policy excerpts with a status line and pauses optional agent investigations.
harbor.failure: Unbounded queues, which trade visible rejections for long delays and cascading failure.

harbor.practice: Harbor fails read-only search over to a second region, but queued write actions have one designated execution owner to avoid duplicates.
harbor.failure: Assuming active-active APIs give consistent business actions across regions.

harbor.practice: Harbor's load test replays logged prompt lengths with an open-loop arrival rate and a mocked model, then benchmarks the real inference pool separately; the two reports are labelled differently.
harbor.failure: Testing with empty prompts and one-token answers.

harbor.practice: If Harbor spends $10 on 100 tasks and 50 succeed, the figure reported is $0.20 per successful task, plus the support cost of fixing the 50 failures.
harbor.failure: Optimising price per call while completion rate falls.

harbor.practice: Harbor's launch review states: "measured 60 RPS on staging with p95 1.8 s for this workload; projected 100 RPS with two more replicas, not yet validated".
harbor.failure: Describing a simulation or extrapolation as a system that served millions of users.
